_comment: SHARED FIXTURE (NRM-5) — two independent implementations must agree on this document.
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/manifest_forms.rs  (what the standalone recovery tool parses)
Web   : nmts/web/test/recovery-map.test.ts   (what the browser writes)
Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
WHAT NRM-5 ADDS: a part stored on Filecoin (NMTS Heavy). Such a part says network 'filecoin',
its blob_id is the piece's PieceCIDv2 string (bafkzcib...), chain names the Filecoin network
('calibration' or 'mainnet'), and copies lists every storage company keeping a whole copy:
its registry number, the data set and piece numbers it proves the piece under (all three as
decimal strings, because the contract counts them as uint256), and the https address it
served the piece from, which ends in /piece/<blob_id>.
WHY THE VERSION MOVED: a reader written for NRM-4 would take the PieceCID to a Walrus
aggregator and be told 'not found' — the same answer as an expired blob. v5 makes it stop on
the document instead.
BOTH SIDES MUST REFUSE: a filecoin part, or chain or copies, in a document declaring v < 5;
chain or copies on a part that is not on filecoin; a filecoin part with no chain, a chain
other than the two, no copies, 0 or more than 12 copies, a blob_id that is not a PieceCIDv2,
a number that is not a canonical decimal uint256, a retrieval_url that is not
https://<host>.../piece/<blob_id>, and a filecoin part in an item placed in a quilt.
The three items: a Walrus file (unchanged by NRM-5), a one-part Heavy file kept at two
companies on Calibration, and a two-part Heavy file on mainnet. The hosts are .example
names and the pieces hold nothing — this exercises the format, not a network.
